newsitem.title: FRANCE: French govt declines comment on France Telecom.
newsitem.headline: French govt declines comment on France Telecom.

text.p: A French finance ministry official declined comment on Wednesday on a newspaper report that the government was considering selling a bigger than expected stake in France Telecom in May.

Financial daily Les Echos said the government, taking advantage of good stock market conditions, could sell between 25 and 35 percent of the telecommunications company, compared to a 20 to 25 percent stake initially planned.
The sale would raise 35 billion to 45 billion francs -- money needed by the government to pay for capital injections into other state-owned companies.

The newspaper said sale process would begin next week with the presentation of France Telecom accounts to stock analysts. The shares would be sold simultaneously in Paris and New York, so U.S. rules would determine the timetable for the sale, the paper said.
Bookbuilding for institutional buyers and pre-marketing for retail investors would start around May 12 and the sale would take place some 10 days later.
The French finance ministry official was asked by reporters to comment on the newspaper report at a meeting of the French and German finance ministers and central bank heads in Lyon, central France.
